regimens.dose_text: Transdermal patch: Initial dose 4.6 mg/24 hours patch applied once daily to clean, intact skin. After a minimum of 4 weeks, increase to recommended maintenance dose of 9.5 mg/24 hours. May increase to 13.3 mg/24 hours in severe dementia. Rotate application sites daily (upper/lower back, upper arm, chest); do not apply to same site for 14 days. Transdermal formulation significantly reduces gastrointestinal adverse effects.

regimens.indication: Mild, Moderate, or Severe Alzheimer's Disease Dementia (Transdermal Patch)

refs.quote: EXELON PATCH is indicated for the treatment of dementia of the Alzheimer’s type (AD).
Initial Dose: Initiate treatment with 4.6 mg/24 hours EXELON PATCH.

regimens.dose_text: Apply one 4.6 mg/24h transdermal patch once daily for at least 4 weeks; if well tolerated, increase to 9.5 mg/24h (standard effective maintenance dose). May further titrate to 13.3 mg/24h for severe dementia. Rotate application site daily (upper back, lower back, upper arm, or chest); do not reapply to same site within 14 days.

There are no adequate data on the developmental risks associated with the use of EXELON in pregnant women. In animals, no adverse effects on embryo-fetal development were observed at oral doses 2-4 times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) (see Data) .

tier.note: No adequate human pregnancy data to establish safety; animal studies showed no adverse embryo-fetal effects at 2-4x MRHD.

pregnancy_pk.value: Lacks adequate human pregnancy data (primarily prescribed in older postmenopausal populations); reserve only if clear maternal benefit outweighs unknown fetal risk.

refs.quote: lack adequate human pregnancy data (`caution` — largely indicated in older postmenopausal populations); anti-amyloid IgG1 antibodies cross the placenta in late pregnancy via FcRn and carry prolonged washout considerations if ever used in reproductive-age carriers.

Oral administration of rivastigmine to pregnant rats and rabbits throughout organogenesis produced no adverse effects on embryo-fetal development up to the highest dose tested (2.3 mg/kg/day), which is 2 and 4 times, respectively, the MRHD of 12 mg per day on a body surface area (mg/m 2 ) basis.

[ropinirole] Relative Infant Dose (RID): Human breast milk concentrations are unstudied, and ropinirole potently suppresses maternal prolactin secretion. Summar

There are no data on the presence of rivastigmine in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects of rivastigmine on milk production. Rivastigmine and its metabolites are excreted in rat milk following oral administration of rivastigmine; levels of rivastigmine plus metabolites in rat milk are approximately 2 times that in maternal plasma.
